# AI and the Human Factor: Neuroscience, Radical Accessibility (A11Y.md) and Community

The video analyzes the work of designer Felipe A. Carriço: AI accelerates the production of interfaces, but human cognition remains the same. Shows A11Y.md, an open protocol that makes code agents follow WCAG 2.2 AA from the first line, and the AmigUX community, made of horizontal conversations and mentoring.

Video by Maurício Yokoyama Issei, published on September 30, 2026 (7 min 47 s).
Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BNaAVW4VI7Y

_The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets, such as [04:12], point to the excerpt of the video._

## AI exponential, paleolithic brain

The video deals with the shock between technological acceleration and the limits of human nature [00:00]. The analysis follows the trajectory, research and philosophy of designer Felipe A. Carriço: anchoring digital development in neurobiological reality, rather than following the blind algorithms [00:20].

The central tension: AI generates interfaces, texts and code at an exponential speed, but the brain that needs to use all this is the same biology of the Paleolithic [00:41]. According to the video, this contrast explains much of the digital exhaustion [01:01].

Think of a scale. AI does not tire out and scale production without limit; human cognition has strict bottlenecks of attention and visual perception. If the design only looks at the speed of the AI, the result is mental overload and exhaustion for the user [01:22].

## What neuroscience imposes on design

Video cites search "Projecting realities", which Felipe presented at PUCRS in 2025. The senses and neural pathways of memory are fixed paths: dopamine, consolidation in the hippocampus and the load of decisions in the prefrontal cortex do not change because a new AI came out [01:45].

To ignore neuroscience is to try to pass the ocean of the internet through a narrow biological funnel [02:06].

Felipe summarizes the risk in a sentence: "vibe coding is only vibing for those who know coding". Asking AI to create systems only by intuition, without understanding the technical basis and the human mind, generates noise and broken interfaces. Those who do not understand what is being built lose control of the tool [02:06].

The rule that comes out: AI is a great means of production, but it is not the goal. Filling a screen with dozens of components generated by the machine, without respecting the time of the brain, destroys usability [02:47].

## The crisis: climbing exclusion

With AI writing interfaces in seconds, an invisible crisis emerges. The AI learns from the current web average, and according to the video, data from WebAIM show that 95.9% of sites have detectable accessibility failures [03:09].

The result is that the AI scale the deletion by default: creates buttons that screen readers do not see and confusing forms faster than any team can fix [03:29].

The market treats accessibility as a late checklist, conferred minutes before launch, often due to fear of process. The proposal of the video is the opposite: accessibility is not final polishing, it is a restriction that exists before the first line of code [03:50].

## A11Y.md: accessibility before prompt

To solve this in practice, the A11Y.md, an open source protocol supported by Anthropic's Claude for Open Source program, appears. According to the video, it was also recognized by Smashing Magazine [04:10].

More than a text file, it is a persistent context system: a behavior contract that requires agents like Cursor, Claude and Copilot to follow the accessibility standards from the beginning [04:10].

Inside the agent, the system rotates in four steps [04:31]:

1. Loads the accessibility context only on demand, so as not to spend tokens for nothing [04:31].
2. Generates the interface already with rigid semantic rules [04:31].
3. It validates the code generated against WCAG 2.2 AA criteria [04:53].
4. It delivers a pending report, so that nothing broken goes on air without human validation [04:53].

The idea comes down to "accessibility before any prompt". Anchoring AI in these principles before she knows what she will build avoids technical errors and ensures that technology breaks down barriers, rather than erecting bigger and faster barriers [05:13].

## AmigUX: the collective response

Besides the code, the technological storm brings professional isolation. The mind and well-being only work well with real human connections, and that's where the AmigUX community comes in [05:34].

The motto is "conversation, not lecture": to remove the ego, to escape from the stages and the marketing of LinkedIn, and to create a space of people interested in people [05:56].

The pillars are horizontality and empathy, without the owner of truth. The conversations are double-handed, and the mentoring is voluntary and direct [05:56].

The greatest merit, according to the video, is a safe psychological space: a junior or a senior can say "I don't know how to do this", admit mistakes and evolve without fear of judgment [06:18].

Direct access to other people is the most valuable asset. Each person is a universe of practical knowledge, and the goal is to connect those who want to teach those who need to learn [06:38]. This exchange likes for real professional relationships and creates a network of protection against the uncertainty that the AI causes [06:58].

## The human factor as anchor

The technology will continue to accelerate, with new AI and frameworks every month. Biology, the ethical need for accessibility and the strength of a community do not change [06:58]. The human factor is the anchor in the middle of the storm [07:19].

The final question: are we designing to feed algorithms or to respect human beings? [07:19]

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is A11Y.md?

An open source protocol that gives code agents a persistent accessibility context, so that they manage and validate interfaces according to WCAG 2.2 AA [04:10].

### Why does AI tend to generate inaccessible interfaces?

Because you learn from the average of the web, and according to the video, 95.9% of sites have detectable accessibility failures [03:09].

## Fonts

- [fecarrico/A11Y.md (GitHub)](https://github.com/fecarrico/A11Y.md): Repository of A11Y.md, by Felipe A. Carriço, MIT license: a context system to build software accessible by default, with rules aligned with WCAG 2.2 AA. The rule in the agent points to a central file, which carries reference guides on demand. Cita Cursor, Claude and Copilot record that the project was selected in July 2026 for the Anthropic Claude for Open Source program.
- [AmigUX](https://amigux.com.br/): Free community site of experience designers, product and service, with WhatsApp group, live dating and mentoring. It is presented as done by people interested in people and describes the meetings as double-handed conversation, not lecture.

## About the video

While Artificial Intelligence has dramatically accelerated the creation of screens and systems, human cognition has remained the same since the paleolithic period. In this explanatory video of 7 1/2 minutes, we explore how the work of **Felipe A. Carriço** (Specialist UX Designer, AI Product Builder and Daltonic) connects Neuroscience, AI Accessibility and Community to ensure that technology continues to serve humans.

Meet the **A11Y.md**, open source protocol of persistent context supported by the programme *Claude for Open Source* Anthropic teaches code agents (Cursor, Claude, Copilot) to build accessible interfaces under the WCAG 2.2 AA standard from the first line. Learn also how to **AmigUX** fosters a network "made by people interested in people", based on horizontal exchanges and free mentoring.
